summary: Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (circa 1967) and the University of Munich, later holding posts at Munich (circa 1981–1993) and Göttingen (circa 1993–2016).

Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (1892–1957) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He served at the University of Calcutta as Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture (attested 1939) and later of History as well (attested 1965).

Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri (born 1925) is a scholar in linguistics and Indology who held the post of professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1991 and 2026).

Hendrik Arent Hamaker (1789–1835) was a linguistics scholar who studied at the Athenaeum Illustre of Amsterdam (circa 1804–1810). He was a professor at the University of Franeker (1815–1817) and Leiden University (1817; 1822–1835).
Hendrik van Gelder (1860–1921) was a history and archaeology scholar. He held posts at Utrecht University from 1906 to 1915 and at Leiden University from 1915 to 1921.

Henepola Gunaratana (b. 1927) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied under Kiribatkumbure Sonuttara and Alagoda Sumanatissa, earning degrees at American University, and held posts at the Buddhist Institute of Kuala Lumpur and American University.

Heng Sure (born 1949) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union under Ronald Y. Nakasone and Hsuan Hua, later holding professorships at GTU, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.
Heng Yin is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Yunnan University (2018–2025) and served as an assistant professor at China West Normal University in 2023.

Henk Blezer (born 1961) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He completed his doctoraal studies at Leiden University (1987–1997) and held positions at Leiden (1993–1997, 2002–2008) and the International Institute for Asian Studies (1997–2001).

Henk Bodewitz (1939–2022) was an Indology scholar who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1963–1973). He held academic posts at Utrecht University (1966; 1976–1992) and Leiden University (~1972–1976; 1992–2002).

Henri Arvon (1914–1992) was a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at the University of Strasbourg, he taught at Prytanée National Militaire, the University of Clermont-Ferrand (1966–1971), and Paris Nanterre University (circa 1971–1982).

Henri Bergson (1859–1941) was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, the École Normale Supérieure (circa 1878–1881), and the University of Paris (circa 1888–1889). He held posts at Lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier (1849–1925) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology educated at Lycée Chaptal. He worked as librarian at the Royal Asiatic Society North China Branch (1871) and held professorships at Sciences Po (~1886–1925) and INALCO (1888).

Henri Deydier (1922–1954) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Jean Przyluski, Henri Maspero, and Alfred Foucher, completed a diploma at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1945–1950), and joined the EFEO in 1950.

Henri Frei (1899–1980) was a linguist and Japanologist. He studied at the University of Geneva under Charles Bally and Manu Leumann, and at INALCO. He held posts at Peking University (1933–1934) and the University of Geneva (1940–1969).

Henri Gaidoz (1842–1932) worked in linguistics, religious studies, and other fields. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber (1865). He held posts at École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (1876).
Henri Hauvette (1865–1935) studied at the Lycée Louis-le-Grand. He subsequently held academic posts at Grenoble Alpes University (circa 1895–1910) and the University of Paris (circa 1910–1935).

Henri Hubert (1872–1927) was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the ENS and the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, later serving at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École du Louvre (1906), and EPHE (1907).

Henri Maspero (1883–1945) worked in sinology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied under Édouard Chavannes and Sylvain Lévi, holding posts at the EFEO (1908–1920), Collège de France (1919–1944), EPHE (~1931–1944), and the Sorbonne/University of Paris (~1937–1944).

Henri Massé (1886–1969) worked in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Algiers (circa 1916–1927) and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (circa 1927–1958).
